what_it_does: CXL (Compute Express Link) is a relatively new high-speed connection standard that lets a server attach extra memory chips beyond what fits directly on the motherboard. Because this extra memory is reached through the CXL link rather than the CPU's fastest local path, it is slower — so the system needs to automatically move heavily used data (hot data) to fast local memory and push rarely used data (cold data) to the slower CXL memory. HybridTier tracks both how frequently data has been accessed over a long window (frequency) and how quickly its access rate is changing right now (momentum), giving a richer picture of what is actually hot. To keep the tracking itself from wasting too much memory and slowing down the processor's own fast cache, HybridTier uses compact probabilistic data structures — small summaries that trade a tiny bit of accuracy for dramatically lower overhead.
